title: CmdPal: Context menus open below the dock flyout

judgment.rationale: Investigate surface ownership and activation ordering, not merely menu placement or a global always-on-top workaround. Current source already resolves an anchor and prepares the popup for its placement target; a missing XamlRoot or deferred-request cancellation must not be assumed.
evidence: The developer report supplies two screenshots showing partial and near-complete occlusion by the parent surface.
The sequence is intermittent; the report does not say which activation/input ordering creates the hidden menu.
Upstream main 9e6593c34949: src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/Services/ContextMenuHost.Flyouts.cs: The surface host chooses the explicit/default anchor and opens the reusable flyout with ShowAt.
Upstream main 9e6593c34949: src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/Controls/ContextMenuFlyout.xaml.cs: ShowAt calls UIHelper.PreparePopupForShow using the loaded placement target before opening.

Upstream main 9e6593c34949: src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/Services/ContextMenuHost.cs: Deferred keyboard opens already use request-version invalidation; simple absence of cancellation is not a supported diagnosis.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce Command Palette menu occlusion behavior

fix_assessment.rationale: Conditional lightweight proposal, not an implementation-grade design. Occlusion is demonstrated, but current source already contains owner preparation and cancellation safeguards; the failing order is unknown.

proposed_fixes.title: Keep a surface's context menu above its owning Dock/palette surface
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: an activation or host-owner ordering race leaves the menu below its visible owning surface despite valid placement preparation. The actual HWND/XamlRoot or z-order transition has not been captured.
plan: Reproduce mouse and keyboard menu opens from Dock and palette separately while recording the owning surface, placement target, popup/root and activation order.
Test rapid summon/deactivate/reopen and menu-near-screen-edge cases to separate occlusion from placement.
Fix the identified owner/activation transition without making every popup globally topmost or weakening light-dismiss behavior.
verification: Context menus remain above their owning surface, including screen-edge placement and repeated summon transitions.
Keyboard focus, light dismissal, submenus and other app windows keep their expected ordering.

confidence.rationale: Occlusion is demonstrated, but current source already contains owner preparation and cancellation safeguards; the failing order is unknown.

prerequisites: Use a disposable test account or controlled test machine; preserve existing user data.
steps: Open equivalent context menus through mouse and keyboard from Dock and palette surfaces, including rapid summon and dismissal.
